title: DeepYellow reclaim rule file
description: One file of reclaim rules. Each rule says what a place on disk is, how safe it is to remove, and what removal costs.

$schema.description: Points editors at this schema. It has no effect on the app.

version.description: The rule file format version. Always 1.

section.description: The heading and intro shown for this file on the generated rules page.

title.description: The section heading, for example Caches.

intro.description: One or two plain sentences saying what this group of rules covers.

rules.description: The rules in this file, in the order they appear on the rules page.

rule.description: One rule for one place on disk.

id.description: A unique, lowercase, dotted name such as caches.spotify. It must not change once released.

title.description: A short name shown in the app, with no full stop at the end.

pattern.description: The place this rule matches. Start with ~/ for your home folder or / for an absolute path. Use * inside a name, ** for any number of folders, and || to join several paths.

tier.description: How safe removal is. safe: regenerates with no visible loss. rebuild: recoverable at a cost of time, network or a login. review: may hold personal data, so the user must look. never: not offered for removal.

whatItIs.description: One plain sentence saying what lives here, ending with a full stop.

consequence.description: What the user loses or waits for if they remove it, with concrete numbers where you have them. End with a full stop.

sideCondition.description: A condition to meet before removing, such as closing the app. Use null when there is none.

cleanupCommand.description: The official cleanup command, shown to the user and never run by DeepYellow. Use null when there is none.

ownerBundleIDs.description: Bundle IDs of the apps that own this place, such as com.spotify.client. Use an empty list when no app owns it.

source.description: Where the claim comes from, such as a vendor page or a test you ran. Safe and rebuild rules need one.

method.description: relaunch-test: you removed it and relaunched the app. vendor-doc: the vendor documents it. location: the place is known by where it sits. research: notes that nobody has verified.

appVersion.description: The app version you tested, for example 1.2.3.

macOSVersion.description: The macOS version you tested on, for example 15.5.

measuredOn.description: The date of the test, as YYYY-MM-DD.

observed.description: What you saw after removing it and relaunching, with sizes and times where you have them.
